question.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t],$ the vector space of polynomials of degree at most $2$ with real coefficients. Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=p(-1)q(-1)+p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1),
$$

find the distance between $p(t)=5t$ and the subspace spanned by $q(t)=t-1$ with respect to the inner product.
question.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $p(t)$ onto $\text{Span}\{q(t)\}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{q(t)}\,p(t) & =\frac{⟨p(t),q(t)⟩}{⟨q(t),q(t)⟩}\,q(t) \\  & =\frac{p(-1)q(-1)+p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1)}{q(-1)q(-1)+q(0)q(0)+q(1)q(1)}\cdot q(t) \\  & =\frac{{\sum }_{i\in \{-1,0,1\}}(5t){|}_{t=i}\cdot (t-1){|}_{t=i}}{{\sum }_{i\in \{-1,0,1\}}(t-1){|}_{t=i}\cdot (t-1){|}_{t=i}}\cdot (t-1) \\  & =\frac{(-5)\cdot (-2)+0\cdot (-1)+5\cdot 0}{(-2)\cdot (-2)+(-1)\cdot (-1)+0\cdot 0}\cdot (t-1) \\  & =\frac{10}{5}\cdot (t-1) \\  & =2(t-1).\end{aligned}
$$

 

The distance between $p(t)=5t$ and the subspace spanned by $q(t)=t-1$ with respect to our inner product is

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =‖p(t)-{\text{proj}}_{q(t)}\,p(t)‖ \\  & =‖5t-2(t-1)‖ \\  & =‖3t+2‖ \\  & =\sqrt{⟨3t+2,3t+2⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the inner product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨3t+2,3t+2⟩ & ={\sum }_{i\in \{-1,0,1\}}(3t+2){|}_{t=i}\cdot (3t+2){|}_{t=i} \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)+2\cdot 2+5\cdot 5 \\  & =1+4+25 \\  & =30.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the distance is $d=\sqrt{30}.$
